questions.prompt: A pixel is given as column u, row v. For an H×W image, indexing is…
questions.explanation: Rows index the first spatial axis and columns the second under this convention.

questions.prompt: An image channel stores each pixel as an unsigned 8-bit integer (uint8). How many distinct values can one such channel represent?
questions.explanation: 8 bits give 2⁸ = 256 distinct values, from 0 to 255.

questions.prompt: An image array has shape (H, W, C) = (2, 3, 3): height, width and channels. How many spatial pixels (positions, ignoring channels) does it contain?
questions.explanation: Spatial pixels = H × W = 2 × 3 = 6. The last axis (3 channels) holds values per pixel and is not counted.

questions.prompt: To normalize a uint8 intensity to [0, 1], divide it by the maximum value 255. What is the normalized value of intensity 255?
questions.explanation: 255 / 255 = 1, the top of the normalized range.

questions.prompt: Build an image inspection script that prints shape, dtype, min, max, and per-channel means. Test RGB-to-BGR conversion by explicit indexing and a round trip. Use synthetic images before downloading data, and record color convention and normalization parameters in the experiment configuration. Explain how camera exposure or lighting shift affects intensity without changing object identity. This is an initial authored lesson; later calibration and vision algorithms depend on additional graph topics.
